This contradicts U.S. media reports alleging critical medical challenges and limited engagement following the attack.

  • Holder catch controversy: 'Sufficient evidence for not out' - Bishop on Patidar wicket

    Former cricketer Ian Bishop believes Rajat Patidar should have been ruled not out after Jason Holder's controversial catch. Bishop cited insufficient control and doubt about the ball touching the ground, suggesting the umpire should have reviewed more closely. Patidar's dismissal significantly impacted RCB's innings.

  • Watch: J&K CM Omar Abdullah shares video of bears ‘stealing’ flag at Srinagar golf course

    An unusual sight unfolded at Srinagar's Royal Spring Golf Course. Two bears entered the premises and made off with a flag. Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah shared a video of the incident online. The bears' playful act amused onlookers. The golf course's proximity to forests often leads to wildlife sightings.

  • CEO says ‘When Google CEO agrees with Elon, everyone must pay attention’; Musk responds

    Elon Musk agreed with a post highlighting Google CEO Sundar Pichai's vision of space-based data centers becoming "the new normal" within a decade. This aligns with Musk's own long-held views on utilizing space for large-scale infrastructure. Pichai previously mentioned Google's "moon shot" to place data centers in orbit to harness solar energy, with a first step planned for 2027.

  • Will not contest a Pawar family member again, says Baramati MP Supriya Sule

    Baramati MP Supriya Sule announced she will not contest elections against any Pawar family member in the future, opting for a different constituency if necessary. Her sister-in-law, Sunetra Pawar, welcomed the decision, emphasizing the importance of separating politics and family relations. This comes after two instances of Pawar family members contesting against each other.

  • ACP-rank officer arrested for 'flashing' at 9-year-old girl in Mumbai

    A senior police officer in Mumbai faces serious charges after allegedly exposing himself to a nine-year-old girl in a Worli garden. Arrested following a complaint, the assistant commissioner of police has been booked under molestation and POCSO Act provisions. He has been remanded to judicial custody as investigations continue into the disturbing incident.

  • ‘Touched me 10 times’: Viral Kumbh girl files POCSO case against film director

    Ernakulam Central police have registered a case against a film director under the Pocso Act following a complaint from the 'viral Kumbh Mela girl'. She alleges the director misbehaved with her when she was a minor, exploiting her for acting opportunities. The alleged incident occurred outside Kerala and the case will be transferred.

  • American billionaire Mark Cuban to engineers: Use these 3 Claude prompts to sharpen your skills

    Mark Cuban urges engineers to master AI, particularly by practicing with Claude. He suggests three prompts to build practical business agents, highlighting opportunities for young professionals to implement AI for cost savings and efficiency. Despite AI's rapid disruption and challenges like cost and reliability, Cuban emphasizes adaptation for competitive advantage.

  • ‘Patriot’ X review: Mammootty and Mohanlal reunion impresses fans

    Mahesh Narayanan's 'Patriot' has made its debut in cinemas, bringing Mammootty and Mohanlal back together for the first time in 18 years. The Voice of Conscience

The charkha as a weapon
Margaret Bourke-White
(Photographer)
TOI take:
Published on: Jan 22, 2026
While imprisoned at Yeravda Jail in Pune from 1932 to 1933, Mahatma Gandhi turned confinement into resistance, urging Indians to spin their own cloth as a rejection of British rule. When photographer Margaret Bourke-White arrived to capture his portrait, she was first required to learn how to use a charkha. The iconic portrait of Gandhi reading beside his wheel became an enduring symbol of his pacifist philosophy and non-violent civil disobedience.
'The last Jew in Vinnitsa'
1941
TOI take:
Published on: Jan 21, 2026
Found in a German soldier’s album, this 1941 photograph titled "The Last Jew in Vinnitsa" captures an Einsatzgruppe D member executing a Ukrainian man. This chilling image documents the Holocaust in Ukraine, where nearly one million Jews were murdered by Nazi forces, including the German Army and auxiliary groups.
A satellite’s unlikely ride
1981
TOI take:
Published on: Nov 21, 2025
On June 19, 1981, Isro launched its first communication satellite, Apple, aboard Ariane-1 from Kourou in French Guiana. This satellite, iconically, was transported on a bullock cart—a reflection of Isro's humble beginnings—just six years after Aryabhatta, when both the agency and the nation’s infrastructure were still developing.
